My plan is to evaluate the single story AMSD-2041, "[GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS," and decide which spec agents to assign.

This story has empty acceptance criteria, no dependencies, no existing spec, and involves live preview functionality across three surfaces (GO, UP, MX) — that signals complexity and cross-cutting concerns. Live preview typically involves real-time content rendering, iframe/proxy handling, state synchronization, and security considerations around untrusted content rendering. With zero acceptance criteria, it needs both requirements elaboration (openspec) and testability/security hardening (speckit). I will assign both agents with openspec first, then speckit, and mark priority as high.

I will know I'm wrong if the story turns out to be trivial or already hand-curated (it is not — spec is null and AC is empty). The output must be raw JSON matching the provided schema, which my plan satisfies by producing a single-element array with both agents listed in order.

**PLAN:**

This story requests "Live Preview of Content in CMS" — a new capability where content editors see real-time updates as they edit in Contentstack. This is **novel**, not a defect.

The attachment point is `useContent` (src/hooks/useContent.ts:5) — it's the central content provider used by 236 callers. Every Contentstack component (`ContentstackLink`, `ContentstackImage`, `ContentstackTable`, etc.) goes through `getContentByKey`. Live preview must plug into this hook so all downstream consumers automatically refresh when CMS content changes without modifying each component.

Since acceptance criteria are empty and the description is just the title, I must derive VCs from the description alone — focusing on what an editor/tester observes: content changes in the CMS appear in the preview without a full page reload. I'll note the Contentstack unreachability constraint and write VCs to our side of the boundary.

I'll know I'm wrong if `useContent` is not actually the single content gateway (but 236 callers strongly suggest it is), or if there's already a preview mechanism I've missed (none visible in the shown code).

The `useContent` hook (236 callers) is the central content delivery mechanism. The root cause is almost certainly in the content-fetching layer — either `useContent` itself or the underlying API client that calls Contentstack — which likely doesn't pass the preview/draft parameters Contentstack requires for live preview. I'll examine `useContent` first, then trace down to the Contentstack API client to find where preview support is missing.
